page1.name: T1
page1.text:
March, 1880
We're ready to say good-bye to city life on the East Coast.  We'll travel first by train and then by covered wagon to the High Plains of Kansas. Once we're there, we'll stake a claim for a homestead of 160 acres. Our family is ready to go west and make a new start!

page2.name: T2
page2.text:
April, 1880
We've finally made it to Kansas!  We've found a  good spot for our homestead, not far from a creek  and a small town.  Until we build a house, we're  living in a tent made from the top of our covered wagon.  Once we get settled, we'll get ready to farm our homestead.

sharedPageDefaults.name: MyText
sharedPageDefaults.text:
March, 1880
We're ready to say good-bye to city life on the East Coast.  We'll travel first by train and then by covered wagon to the High Plains of Kansas. Once we're there, we'll stake a claim for a homestead of 160 acres. Our family is ready to go west and make a new start!

April, 1880
We've finally made it to Kansas!  We've found a  good spot for our homestead, not far from a creek  and a small town.  Until we build a house, we're  living in a tent made from the top of our covered wagon.  Once we get settled, we'll get ready to farm our homestead.

generalCaptions.name: ATexts
generalCaptions.text: We're so proud of our youngest daughter.
We're so proud of our eldest son.
Our neighbors helped us build this sod house in just one day!
We finally covered our sod walls with wooden planks. Now it feels like a real house.
Things have been going very well on the homestead.  Now we live in this new house instead of our old one.
We've been living on the homestead for five years now. According to the Homestead Act, now the land is really ours!
Before we built our well, we had to carry pails of water from the creek every day.
Our team of horses sure have a good appetite at the end of a day's work in the fields.
Some folks use oxen instead of horses to pull their hay wagon.
We finally had enough money to buy some furniture from the store.
Farming is much easier with a big  steam-engine tractor.
The general store sells just about anything you'd want to buy.
Plowing this hard, dry soil is not easy.
Our windmill pumps water from deep underground.
Out here, a town can be built in just a day or two.
We're just starting out, so we made nearly  everything we own with our own hands.
There's nothing as exciting as watching the 12:05 roar into town.  Who knows which letters, packages, or visitors will be on board?
There's plenty of open space on the Great Plains for farmers, cowboys, and their herds of cattle.
This winter there's plenty of hay for our horses and cows.
This year, three generations of our family sat down to a big Thanks giving dinner.
We miss our eldest daughter, who lives with her husband in Detroit.
This year, our first son was born!
This year, our second son was born!
This year, our second daughter was born!

generalCaptions.name: ATextsE
generalCaptions.text: We're so proud of our younger son.

datedCaptions.name: T18834
datedCaptions.text: The Brooklyn Bridge in New York City is finally ready. If our creek were as wide as New York's East River, we'd have all the water we need.

datedCaptions.name: T18858
datedCaptions.text:
August, 1885
Buffalo Bill's Wild West show came to town. Someone threw a playing card in the air and Annie Oakley shot it ten times.  What a show!

datedCaptions.name: T188612
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1886
The snowstorms started early this year, and they sure are fierce. I think we're in for a long, cold winter.

datedCaptions.name: T189012
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1890
In Wounded Knee, South Dakota, the U.S. Calvary killed about 200 Sioux Indians who had no weapons. Why did this tragedy happen?

datedCaptions.name: T189412
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1894
The railroad strikes had me worried.  I thought I wouldn't be able to send my crops to the dealer. Luckily,  the strike was over by harvest time.

datedCaptions.name: T189612
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1896
There's another gold rush. This time it's up in Canada, near the Klondike River.  Cousin George went up there, but we stayed here in Kansas.

datedCaptions.name: T18988
datedCaptions.text:
August, 1898
In faraway Cuba, Teddy Roosevelt's Rough Riders charged up San Juan Hill.  We won Cuba from the Spanish, but we won't keep it.

datedCaptions.name: T18974
datedCaptions.text:
April, 1897
Immigrants from Russia brought a new kind of wheat to plant here.  It's called "Turkey Red," and it grows well in dry soil like ours.

datedCaptions.name: T190312
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1903
The Wright brothers went up in their flying machine in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The only flying machine in Kansas is a tractor in a tornado!

datedCaptions.name: T190511
datedCaptions.text:
Novermber, 1905
We've put Teddy Roosevelt back in the White House. He understands the farmers in the Great Plains. He wants to help us find more water.

datedCaptions.name: T19065
datedCaptions.text:
May, 1906
Cousin George was in San Francisco last  month for the big earthquake. He was so scared that he's moving back to Kansas!

datedCaptions.name: T19084
datedCaptions.text:
April, 1908
The Ford Company put out a new car, the Model T. It's a good, solid car. Some folks are even using it to pull their plows!

datedCaptions.name: T19098
datedCaptions.text:
August, 1909
We were glad when Congress passed the Enlarged Homestead Act, but most of our friends think that a 320-acre farm is still too small!

datedCaptions.name: T19114
datedCaptions.text:
April, 1911
The F.W. Woolworth Company Inc. opened a "5-and-dime" store in town.  There are over 1,000 Woolworth stores across the country.

datedCaptions.name: T19125
datedCaptions.text:
May, 1912
Last month, the Titanic sank.  More than 1,000 people drowned, including a few millionaires. It just goes to show that money isn't everything.

datedCaptions.name: T191311
datedCaptions.text:
November, 1913
Congress passed the 16th Amendment. Now we have to pay income tax. I don't mind, as long as I don't have to fill out a lot of long forms.

datedCaptions.name: T19164
datedCaptions.text:
April, 1916
Germany has been threatening our ships. People say that we're about to enter the Great War.

datedCaptions.name: T191812
datedCaptions.text:
December, 1918
The war is over, and Cousin George is coming home from France. He kept his head down during the shooting, but he's getting a medal.
